ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against PEP lists maintained by TRACFIN (French FIU), EU consolidated list, UN sanctions, and OFAC SDN; domestic sanctions screening under Code monétaire et financier

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II: Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (common incorporation provisions) and Articles L.227-1 to L.227-31 (Société par Actions Simplifiée specific regime); implementing regulation R.224-9 (escrow deposit of cash contributions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) - Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (electronic single window, formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); substantive RCS registration executed by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) constituting the company, filed electronically with the Guichet Unique, together with the electronic declaration replacing the former Cerfa M0 form and annexes (JAL publication attestation, capital deposit certificate, beneficial-owner declaration).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum share capital for an SAS (Article L.227-2 Code de commerce); capital may be set at EUR 1 and is freely fixed by the Statuts. For cash contributions, at least 50% of the subscribed amount must be paid up on incorporation into a blocked escrow account held with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the balance must be paid within 5 years. In-kind contributions must be fully delivered at incorporation and, where statutory thresholds are reached, appraised by a commissaire aux apports. Escrowed funds are released only upon presentation of the Kbis extract evidencing RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF [NAME] SAS. The shareholders unanimously resolve and declare: (1) Approval of the Articles of Association (Statuts), which constitute the sole constitutive act of the Société par Actions Simplifiée governed by Articles L.227-1 to L.227-31 of the French Commercial Code. (2) Full subscription of the share capital in accordance with the Statuts; the Chairman certifies that the statutory proportion of cash contributions has been deposited in escrow under Article L.227-2 of the Code de commerce. (3) Establishment of the registered office at the address stated in the Statuts, within the jurisdiction of the competent Commercial Court. (4) Appointment of [Name] as President of the company. (5) Authorization to the President to publish the legal announcement, to file the electronic dossier with the INPI Guichet Unique, and to complete all incorporation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Statuts and publication of the legal notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized by the Préfecture in the department of the registered office; notaire only mandatory if real-estate in-kind contributions are made
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts containing corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose restricted to AI data labeling, data curation and BPO services, duration (99 years), share capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, and powers of the President. Have all shareholders sign the Statuts (private seal or notarized where required) with each page initialed. Publish a formation notice in an approved JAL giving the corporate name, form, registered office, share capital and purpose, and obtain the attestation de parution.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts (sous seing privé or authenticated)
Passport or national ID of each shareholder
Proof of residential address of each shareholder issued within the last 6 months
Draft beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Attestation de parution issued by the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL refuses publication, correct the notice and republish; if the corporate purpose is deemed imprecise, amend the objet social clause with counsel and obtain a new attestation; any defect in shareholder identity documentation must be cured before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of subscribed cash capital into a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company in formation; transfer at least 50% of the cash capital subscriptions and obtain the certificat du dépositaire / attestation de dépôt de fonds. Funds remain frozen until the Kbis extract is produced. If in-kind contributions exist, attach the contribution report and verify that title has been fully transferred before registration.
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt de fonds (deposit certificate)
Subscription list (liste des souscriptions)
Copy of bank account opening documentation
Contribution report by commissaire aux apports (if thresholds exceeded)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit, correct the account naming (exact legal form and company name) and resubmit; where the deposit certificate contains errors, request a rectified certificate prior to filing; in-kind contribution disputes are cured by a supplementary contribution report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the incorporation dossier to the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI - Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (electronic portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the portal, create the company-formation application, enter the SAS data (name, form, registered office, purpose, share capital, subscription allocations, President details), declare the beneficial owners, attach all documents, pay the state fees (approximately EUR 126.17, comprising greffe fees, greffe tax, BODACC insertion and disbursements, plus JAL costs of EUR 190-220), and validate the application electronically. Retain the certificat de dépôt with its submission reference.
required_dossiers: Electronic creation declaration (former Cerfa M0 equivalent)
Final signed Statuts (PDF)
Attestation de parution from the JAL
Attestation de dépôt de fonds / certificat du dépositaire
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs
Statement of non-conviction of the President (déclaration sur l'honneur)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any notice of non-conformity within the 15-day period through the portal; correct the Statuts, re-sign any amended pages and resubmit; if the portal transmission fails three times, file a paper dossier directly with the competent Greffe; request supervisory intervention through the INPI support channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The verified dossier is transmitted automatically to the Greffe, which conducts a 24-hour legal review. Upon approval, the company is registered in the RCS and assigned its SIREN and SIRET numbers (APE code 63.11Z). The temporary registration certificate is issued immediately, and the definitive Kbis extract is delivered within 48 hours. The escrowed share capital is then released to the President upon presentation of the Kbis.
required_dossiers: Validation file forwarded by the Guichet Unique
Copy of the attestation de parution
Copy of the deposit certificate
Proof of registered-office domiciliation (bail or domiciliation agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a demande de complément, respond within the deadline with corrected documentation. In case of refusal to register, apply to the President of the Tribunal Judiciaire in référé to order registration, or correct the defective clauses and resubmit the dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon Kbis issuance, URSSAF registration is finalized automatically and the SIREN/SIRET numbers are confirmed. If employees are engaged, file the Déclaration Préalable à l'Embauche (DPAE) before commencement of work, draft the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), and verify electrical and fire-safety compliance of the premises. Maintain GDPR compliance for data-labeling operations and, where contractually required, implement ISO 27001 / ISO 42001 management systems.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
URSSAF identification notice
Déclaration Préalable à l'Embauche (DPAE) for each employee
Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP)
Records of fire-safety equipment checks and electrical installation conformity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF fails to generate the identification notice, contact the local URSSAF with the Kbis reference; where DREETS identifies workplace-safety deficiencies, implement corrective actions within the prescribed delay and produce updated compliance records; late DPAE filings are regularized with a retroactive declaration subject to potential administrative fines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 8220 office-based services; workplace and labor oversight is exercised by DREETS (Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités) and fire prevention by the local SDIS (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours); the company registers under APE code 63.11Z (data processing, hosting and related activities).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required - data labeling, RLHF curation and AI-training BPO constitute a free-access service activity (activité libre) under French law; no sectoral operating or manufacturing permit is required. Registration in the RCS with extraction of the Kbis constitutes the sole operating authorization, supplemented by voluntary ISO 27001 / ISO 42001 certification and GDPR compliance for client assurance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement) - Ministry of Ecological Transition
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based BPO and data-labeling activities do not appear in the ICPE nomenclature (Article R.511-9 Code de l'environnement); no environmental impact assessment and no case-by-case examination (examen au cas par cas) is required. A full EIA would be triggered only if the building project itself exceeded urban-planning or ICPE thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges or VOC emissions; premises are limited to domestic wastewater discharged into the municipal sewer network under the arrêté du 21 juillet 2015 governing non-domestic connections. Electronic waste (DEEE/WEEE) must be handled in accordance with Directive 2012/19/EU and Decree No. 2005-829, with traceability certificates archived for each disposal operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before employees enter the premises, the employer must draft the DUERP (Articles L.4121-1 et seq. Code du travail), maintain a fire-safety register (registre de sécurité), and ensure electrical installations conform to NF C 15-100 with annual equipment checks. For office buildings not open to the public, no ERP classification applies; if any part is open to the public, an ERP 5th-category conformity declaration must be submitted to the SDIS. Structural load certification is recommended for any server room to validate floor capacity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French-resident entities register for SIREN/SIRET through the guichet unique; non-resident entities with French operations must appoint a fiscal representative and register for SIREN via DGFiP procedures
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections; hybrid mismatch elections governed by EU ATAD and French domestic rules for interest, royalties, and services

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing (facturation électronique) for all B2B transactions via the national platform since 2024; digital stamping and clearance through DGFiP with API integration requirements

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate for goods physically exported outside the EU or services performed for non-EU customers; requires proof of export or customer location outside EU
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or proof of non-EU payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties of up to 40% of evaded VAT plus interest and potential criminal sanctions for fraudulent zero-rating claims; retrospective clawback of zero-rated VAT with audit adjustments

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full convertibility for both current account transactions and capital movements pursuant to EU regulations and national legislation. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without quantitative restrictions, subject only to standard corporate tax compliance, beneficial ownership verification, and anti-money laundering reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must repatriate foreign currency proceeds from sales to non-EU destinations within six months of shipment date. Mandatory surrender to an authorised French bank at the official exchange rate is required unless a specific authorisation for delayed surrender or retention is granted by the Banque de France. Intra-EU trade proceeds are exempt from surrender requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for digital electronic money institutions including PayPal and Wise for cross-border payouts, subject to French Payment Services Directive compliance, local payment institution licensing, and ongoing AML monitoring.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and video identification permitted for French SAS entities under Banque de France guidelines; physical appearance required only for high-value accounts or elevated risk profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared business purpose and source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements, director declarations, bank reference letters, and independent source-of-wealth verification

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership or director links to high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence including PEP screening, third-party ownership certificates, and legal entity verification reports

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 100 (Capital Contribution) or 101 (Equity Injection). All transactions require KYC/AML verification, source-of-funds documentation, and Banque de France reporting for amounts exceeding €50,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing via SWIFT MT103 for commercial payments or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit for trade settlements. All disbursements must be supported by commercial invoices, purchase orders, and VAT-compliant documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval and deposit at the RCS ('dépôt des comptes annuels') — statutory financial statements, management report, and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI Guichet Unique (French corporate registries)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; accounts must be deposited with the RCS within 1 month after approval, unless the Commercial Court grants an extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit exposes the company to a formal request to regularize, a court-imposed daily penalty ('astreinte'), fines up to EUR 1,500, public listing in BODACC, and, after persistent default, judicial strike-off ('radiation') from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return ('déclaration de résultats' — forms 2065/2065-SD and attached 'liasse fiscale')
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP — French tax administration, filed electronically via 'impot.gouv.fr' / EFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year entity, due by the third business day following 1 May; for an off-calendar-year entity, due by the third business day following six months from fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on tax due (40% for bad faith, 80% for abusive understatement), monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%, and possible automatic assessment and enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business property contribution ('Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises' — CFE) declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP / Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) of the business establishment location
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Existing establishments as at 1 January of the year must file the annual return (Form 1327-CFE) by the early December filing deadline and pay the assessed CFE by 15 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or pay on time generates late-payment penalties of 10%, 25%, or 40%, plus monthly late-payment interest, administrative enforcement by tax attachment, and loss of any threshold-based relief.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner (RBE) declaration update — 'déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs' in case of shareholding changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS registry via INPI Guichet Unique; no separate DGFiP filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any effective change in beneficial ownership, including a share transfer; no standalone annual filing is due if the beneficial owner data remains unchanged.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the RBE declaration is punishable under the Monetary and Financial Code by fines up to EUR 22,500 for natural persons and EUR 112,500 for legal entities, plus possible imprisonment for natural persons; the company may also be prevented from invoking its rights against third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' collective decision approving the annual accounts and internal statutory-register audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate minutes kept at the registered office; financial statements are subsequently transmitted to the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Collective decision must be made within 6 months of fiscal year-end; the share ledger, minute books, RBE record, and auditor reports should be checked before the approval meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent failure to hold the approval decision within the legal window blocks the annual accounts deposit, exposes the president to court-convening orders at the request of a shareholder or creditor, and may support an application for judicial removal from the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS must appoint a statutory auditor ('commissaire aux comptes') when it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at fiscal year-end: total balance sheet greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover greater than EUR 8,000,000; more than 50 average employees. A shareholder holding at least 10% of capital may also request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP ('règlement ANC 2016-07', as amended, and the French Commercial Code); IFRS as adopted by the EU applies only to consolidated financial statements of listed or required groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law requires the SAS to file a beneficial-owner declaration at inception and to update it within 30 days of any change. There is no annual UBO re-filing when no shareholding or beneficial-ownership change occurs. As governance best practice, the president should reconcile the share ledger and RBE filing at the annual accounts approval meeting and submit an update if the recorded data is stale.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share-ledger / securities-movement register ('registre des mouvements de titres')
Shareholders' decisions minute book ('registre des décisions collectives / procès-verbaux')
Attendance sheets and powers of attorney for any general meeting ('feuille de présence et pouvoirs')
Beneficial-owner declaration and supporting proof of RBE filing ('déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs')

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 – USD 800 per year for commercial domiciliation or a registered-office service in France; Paris central locations range from USD 500 to USD 1,500.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 15,000 for a typical statutory audit by a French 'commissaire aux comptes'; the fee depends on revenue, deliverable scope, group structure, and transaction volume.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. A 3.3% social contribution may apply to companies whose corporate income tax exceeds EUR 763,000, subject to the statutory turnover threshold and other conditions, producing an overall rate of approximately 25.83%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, generally subject to turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up capital, and qualifying ownership conditions. The French Patent Box regime may apply a separate 10% rate to qualifying net income from patents and comparable intellectual property. Research and development expenditure may qualify for the French research tax credit, generally at 30% of eligible expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to statutory eligibility and substantiation. The Innovation Tax Credit may be available to qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises for eligible innovation expenditure.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited. Utilization is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million in the relevant year. Loss carryback is generally available for the preceding financial year, subject to statutory limits and election requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal at impots.gouv.fr using the EDI-TDFC or EFI electronic filing channel. The return is accompanied by the French tax package, generally Forms 2050-SD through 2059-G-SD, and applicable sector-specific schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return. Corporate income tax installments are generally payable quarterly, with an annual balancing payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year. The tax administration's annual filing calendar must be checked for the precise electronic deadline. Corporate income tax installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with the final balance generally due by 15 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax office, financial year opening and closing dates, legal form, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent does not replace the French SAS as the taxpayer. The French SAS reports its own French legal identity, SIREN number, registered office, and French financial year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, taxable profit or loss section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax liability, taxable profit or tax loss, applicable rate, tax credits, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French company's taxable result after French tax adjustments. Do not exclude profit merely because the shareholders, directors, customers, or service providers are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or tax loss, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax adjustments, and temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify related-party charges, foreign taxes, withholding taxes, non-deductible distributions, provisions, interest limitation adjustments, and expenses lacking business purpose or supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening tax losses, losses generated during the period, losses utilized, losses carried forward, and any elected carryback.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain continuity between prior filings and the current return. Cross-border changes in ownership, activity, or business purpose may restrict the use of tax losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2058-C-SD, tax credits and tax receivables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, tax reductions, refundable tax receivables, and amounts carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only credits legally available to the French SAS and retain eligibility evidence, including research records, payroll data, qualifying expenditure schedules, and required certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, income statement, fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, receivables, liabilities, and accounting result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include intercompany loans, trade balances, service charges, royalties, shareholder accounts, foreign-currency balances, and related-party transactions on a consistent accounting basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals of fixed assets, securities, and other business assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French rules to disposals by the French SAS. A non-resident shareholder's disposal of SAS shares is a separate shareholder-level analysis and is not reported as the SAS's operating gain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning transactions and relationships with associated enterprises where the statutory reporting requirements apply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose controlled transactions with foreign parent companies, affiliates, common-control entities, and permanent establishments when required. Ensure consistency with transfer pricing documentation and accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: VAT returns, payroll social contribution declarations, and withholding reporting are separate from the corporate income tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owner does not consolidate VAT, payroll, or withholding obligations into the corporate income tax return. The French SAS remains responsible for French VAT, payroll, and employment reporting where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns may trigger a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% in cases involving deliberate non-compliance after formal notice and potentially to 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive conduct. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Inaccurate returns may trigger reassessment, interest, tax penalties, loss of tax credits, and criminal proceedings in serious fraud cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident legal entity, subject to domestic exemptions, European Union Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, applicable tax treaties, anti-abuse rules, and beneficial ownership requirements. A 12.8% rate generally applies to dividends paid to non-resident individuals, subject to treaty or statutory relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain a valid tax residence certificate from the recipient's foreign tax authority and establish beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose compliance where relevant, and sufficient economic substance. For French-source dividends, interest, or royalties, use the applicable French Forms 5000, 5001, 5002, or 5003, as relevant, for relief at source or refund procedures. The French payer should retain the residence certificate, treaty forms, ownership chain, payment records, board approvals, and anti-abuse analysis. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply to qualifying corporate shareholders meeting minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions. Failure to obtain the documentation before payment may require withholding at the domestic rate followed by a refund claim.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-resident recipients are generally subject to a 25% domestic withholding tax, subject to treaty reduction, EU Interest and Royalties Directive relief, and statutory exemptions. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but special rules may apply to payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, certain financial instruments, or anti-abuse situations. Treaty rates vary by recipient country and beneficial-owner status and must be confirmed under the applicable bilateral convention. The French payer must separately assess deductibility, transfer pricing, interest limitation, anti-hybrid rules, and beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer pricing documentation is generally mandatory for French entities or groups meeting the statutory threshold of EUR 150 million in annual turnover or gross assets, subject to applicable group and ownership conditions. Entities below that threshold must still apply the arm's-length principle and provide adequate evidence during an audit. A simplified transfer pricing statement may be required for covered entities. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups meeting the EUR 750 million consolidated revenue threshold. Transactions of at least EUR 100,000 per category may require inclusion in the annual transfer pricing declaration, subject to the applicable filing rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a separate stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance remains material under the arm's-length principle, French anti-abuse doctrine, the principal-purpose test in treaties, beneficial ownership rules, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, anti-hybrid rules, and general anti-abuse provisions. The French SAS should maintain adequate French decision-making, personnel or genuinely controlled outsourced functions, premises or operational capacity, books and records, commercial rationale, risk control, and authority over the AI data-labeling and BPO activities. Conduit arrangements, artificial management fees, circular cash flows, and entities lacking functional capacity may be recharacterized or denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of turnover, fabricated expenses, false invoices, undeclared distributions, deliberate omission of foreign accounts or controlled transactions, or manipulation of the corporate income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, 40% penalty for deliberate failure, potentially 80% penalty for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive conduct, late-payment interest, and criminal tax-fraud sanctions. Serious tax fraud may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated cases potentially carrying up to seven years and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability where they personally participated in fraud. They may also face civil or tax-debt liability where fraudulent maneuvers or serious and repeated management misconduct caused the company's tax insolvency. Travel restrictions or asset measures may arise in criminal or enforcement proceedings, but are not automatic consequences of an ordinary filing error.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and profit shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially inflated payments to foreign affiliates, unsupported management fees, non-arm's-length royalties, interest exceeding market terms, use of a loss-making French entity to perform valuable functions, or failure to document controlled transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment to arm's-length profit, possible withholding tax reassessment, denial of deductions, late-payment interest, and penalties for inadequate or missing transfer pricing documentation. A documentation-related penalty may be imposed subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts and the value of the reassessed transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for knowingly approving non-arm's-length transactions, especially where records are falsified or assets are diverted. Criminal liability may arise if transfer pricing conduct forms part of tax fraud, fraudulent bankruptcy, money laundering, or abuse of corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, artificial management, or treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the French SAS solely as a conduit, appointing nominal directors, routing dividends or royalties through France without business functions, back-to-back payments, circular funding, or claiming treaty benefits without beneficial ownership or commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or domestic exemptions, withholding tax at the statutory rate, reassessment under the abuse-of-law or anti-abuse rules, penalties, interest, and possible recharacterization of the arrangement or beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement sham arrangements may incur criminal liability for fraud, money laundering, or abuse of corporate assets. Corporate protection does not shield individuals from personal participation in unlawful conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared cross-border payments and withholding tax failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, fees, or other French-source amounts to non-residents without applying required withholding, failing to obtain treaty documentation, or misclassifying royalties as services or reimbursements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, interest, penalties, possible liability of the payer for the tax that should have been withheld, and sanctions for inaccurate or late reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed where they deliberately authorize withholding-tax evasion, conceal the recipient, or falsify payment records. Ordinary technical errors generally create corporate liability rather than automatic personal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fabricated customer invoices, undeclared digital or cross-border services, false input VAT recovery, sham subcontractors, or participation in missing-trader arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, denial of input VAT, penalties potentially reaching 40% or 80% depending on conduct, late-payment interest, joint liability in certain fraudulent chains, and criminal prosecution for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable where they knowingly organized or facilitated VAT fraud. Criminal sanctions may include imprisonment and fines, and courts may order confiscation or other asset measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering, terrorist financing, and payment-rail misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using PayPal, Wise, or bank accounts to receive or distribute unexplained funds, conceal beneficial owners, split payments, recycle proceeds, pay fictitious contractors, or bypass customer due-diligence and sanctions controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Account restrictions, payment suspension, suspicious transaction reporting, asset freezing or confiscation, administrative sanctions, AML fines, and criminal sanctions for money laundering. Money laundering may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with aggravated cases carrying materially higher sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may be prosecuted personally, face asset confiscation, management bans, and restrictions on conducting business. Travel bans may be imposed by judicial order where legally justified; they are not automatic for ordinary AML deficiencies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Payroll, social-security, and undeclared labor violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying employees as contractors, using undeclared workers, underreporting payroll, failing to withhold social contributions, or outsourcing core work without appropriate employment and social-security analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid contributions, surcharges, penalties, employment-law damages, administrative sanctions, possible prohibition from public contracts, and criminal sanctions for concealed work.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted for concealed work or deliberate social-security fraud and may incur civil liability for unpaid contributions and employee damages where statutory conditions are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Accounting falsification and corporate asset misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining false accounts, concealing liabilities, diverting company funds, paying personal expenses from the SAS, approving unsupported related-party charges, or distributing dividends without distributable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of accounts, tax reassessment, repayment of improperly distributed amounts, civil damages, director disqualification, and criminal sanctions for misuse of corporate assets or fraudulent accounting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and de facto managers may be personally liable for restitution, damages, director disqualification, and imprisonment where criminal elements are established. Limited liability does not protect intentional misconduct or misuse of corporate assets.
